images.filename: A Boulder with Plaque in Honor of Januarius MacGahan in Panagyurishte.JPG
images.caption: A Boulder with Commemorative Plaque in memory of Januarius MacGahan on street MacGahan in Panagyurishte, Bulgaria. The inscription on the plaque reads: "To the Memory of the Prominent American Humanist, Selfless Journalist and Friend of the Bulgarian People Januarius Aloysius MacGahan (1844-1878), from his Fellow Countrymen- Volunteers in the Peace Corps, the year 2002."
images.alt: A Boulder with Commemorative Plaque in memory of Januarius MacGahan on street MacGahan in Panagyurishte, Bulgaria. images.filename: Newspaper Correspondents and the War - The Graphic 1877.jpg
images.caption:
Newspaper Correspondents and the War (Russo-Turkish War (1877–1878)). Illustration for The Graphic, 25 August 1877.
Mr. Wentworth Huyshe, New York Herald, (with the Turks); Mr. Melton Prior, artist of the Illustrated News  (with the Turks); Mr. Jourdan, Daily Telegraph (with the Turks); Mr. Archibald Forbes, Daily News (with the Russians); Mr. F Villiers, artist of The Graphic (with the Russians); Mr. J. Ananian, artist of the Graphic (with the Turks); Mr. J.A. Macgahan, Daily News (with the Russians);  Mr. Suter, Daily Telegraph (with the Turks); Mr. Coningsby, Times (with the Turks);  Mr. Camille Barrere,  Manchester Guardian, and Republique Francaise (with the Turks);  Herr Winter, Vienna Tagblatt (with the Turks); Mr. Henry Dymond, Morning Advertiser (with the Turks);  Mr. James Dow, Sheffield Daily Telegraph (with the Turks);  Lieutenant Colonel Brackenbury, Times (with the Russians); Mr. W. Kingston, Daily Telegraph (with the Turks).
Inset: Reception of Artists and Correspondents in Shumla by Mehemet Ali Pasha, the Turkish Commander in Chief.
Signed
